API ​

Mosaic can be used from code through the TypeScript SDK (mosaic-ts, in sdk/ts) and over HTTP. The SDK is what the mosaic CLI is built on, so everything the CLI does is available to your code as well.

Entry pointFor
mosaic-tsReading, writing, packing, federating, selecting and composing archives
mosaic-ts/duckdbLoading archives into DuckDB and querying them with SQL. See Querying with DuckDB
mosaic-ts/apiA typed client and server for the HTTP API. See The HTTP API

WARNING

The SDK is in progress and not yet published to npm. Names and signatures may change.

Reading and writing archives ​

LoadMosaicFile opens the bytes of a .tsr, and WriteMosaicFile turns a MosaicFile back into bytes. A MosaicFile is the index plus the serialized component rows, keyed by type.

ts
import fs from "node:fs";
import { LoadMosaicFile, WriteMosaicFile } from "mosaic-ts";

const file = await LoadMosaicFile(new Uint8Array(fs.readFileSync("house-v1.tsr")));

for (const section of file.index.sections) {
    console.log(section.header.message, section.nodes.length, "nodes");
}

fs.writeFileSync("copy.tsr", await WriteMosaicFile(file));

Packing source documents ​

A source document (.mosaic.json) becomes an archive with packMosaicSource, or straight from disk with packMosaicSourceFile, which is what mosaic pack runs. buildMosaicFile stops at the in-memory MosaicFile.

ts
import { packMosaicSourceFile } from "mosaic-ts";

const result = await packMosaicSourceFile("house-v1.mosaic.json");   // writes house-v1.tsr

Combining files ​

FunctionWhat it does
collapseNodesByPath(file)Every node as it stands after all sections, with later writes winning and DELETEs applied
federate(a, b, keepHistory)Merges b over a. Tables are laid end to end and references shifted; with keepHistory every section is kept
diffFiles(old, new, markMissingAsDelete)The section that turns old into new

Selecting nodes ​

selectNodes takes a subset of a file as a file of its own, made whole: anything a kept component points at comes along. It is the same operation the HTTP API's nodes endpoint performs.

ts
import { selectNodes } from "mosaic-ts";

const { file: subset, missing, pulledIn } = selectNodes(file, {
    nodes: ["70000000-7000-4000-8000-700000000003"],
    componentTypes: ["core::transform", "core::name"],   // all types when left out
    includeChildren: true,                               // and everything beneath
    compose: true,                                       // resolve inheritance first
});

Composing to glTF ​

mosaicToGltf composes a file into a glTF document and its binary chunk, and writeGlb writes those as a .glb. composeArchiveToGlb does the whole thing from a path, following imports, and is what mosaic compose runs. See Composing a GLB for what the composition does.

ts
import { composeArchive, writeGlb } from "mosaic-ts";

const { document, binary, warnings, sources } = await composeArchive("helmet-plaza.tsr");
const glb = writeGlb(document, binary);

FunctionPackageCLI
gltfToMosaicmosaic-tsmosaic gltf
svgToMosaicmosaic-tsmosaic svg-pack
IFC conversionsdk/ifc4mosaic ifc

Typed components ​

The schema constants (CORE_SCHEMAS, GLTF_SCHEMAS, SVG_SCHEMAS) and type ids (CORE_TYPE, GLTF_TYPE, SVG_TYPE) are exported as well. For your own component schemas, code generation produces typed TypeScript or C# classes.
